findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator crashes on DateTimeField order_by
findings.body: The new paginator is used by OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint with order_by="-datetime", but `get_item_key` is copied from `Paginator` and does `math.floor(value)` / `math.ceil(value)` on the raw field value. For `AuditLogEntry.datetime` that value is a `datetime`, and `math.floor(datetime)` raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime`. `build_cursor` calls this key function for the first page, so any authorized request with `optimized_pagination=true` will return a 500 instead of results. It should convert datetimes to epoch milliseconds like `DateTimePaginator` does.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets cause Django negative-slicing error/500
findings.body: In the advanced-feature branch, a forged or malformed cursor with negative `offset` sets `start_offset = cursor.offset` and then slices `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySet does not support negative offsets/indices and raises an exception rather than the Python list semantics implied by the comment. A client can pass a cursor string such as `-1:-1:0` with `optimized_pagination=true` and trigger an internal server error. Negative offsets should be rejected or clamped, as the base paginator now does for non-prev cursors.

findings.title: No tests for the new paginator or gated endpoint
findings.body: This PR adds a new paginator and an opt-in endpoint path but includes no tests. There is no coverage for `OptimizedCursorPaginator` with datetime ordering, cursor navigation, negative/malformed cursor offsets, or the superuser/global-access gating in `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint`. Tests would have caught the datetime key crash and the negative-slice crash before merge.
